messages.content: Do NPTEL courses count towards my graduation credits, and how many minimum credits can I take online?

Yes. NPTEL (and other MOOC/NPTEL) courses are accepted as Programme Elective (PE) or Open Elective (OE) credits toward your B.Tech degree.

A minimum of **12 credits** must be earned through such online platforms to satisfy the graduation requirement.

I want to finish quickly. Can I register for 42 credits this semester?

No. The absolute maximum credit limit per semester is 40 credits. You can register for up to 40 credits this semester and use the full 180‑credit requirement to accelerate your graduation, but 42 credits is strictly prohibited.
My CGPA is 9.2 but I had one backlog in the second semester. Am I eligible for Honours?

No. Honours requires **both** a CGPA ≥ 8.5 **and** having passed every course on the first attempt. Since you have a backlog from the second semester, you are permanently ineligible for Honours, regardless of your 9.2 CGPA.
I am in semester 3 but I have a backlog in semester 1 Applied Physics. Can I register for it?

Yes. Since Applied Physics (APS1112) is a first‑year (Semester 1) course, it can be taken in any later semester, and the parity check confirms that registration is permitted for your current Semester 3 (odd) status.

**What you need to do**

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **Registration mode** | Register in **Mode A** (fulfil attendance and appear in all evaluation components). |
| **Attendance** | Maintain at least 75 % attendance to be eligible for the end‑semester exam (condonation is possible only between 65 %– 75 %). |
| **Credit limit** | Ensure the total credits you register for this semester do not exceed the hard cap of 40 credits. |
| **Backlog policy** | As a backlog, the course must be cleared before you can progress to higher‑level courses that depend on it. |

So you may add APS1112 to your Semester 3 registration, provided you meet the above conditions.

I am in semester 3 but I have a backlog in semester 1 Applied Physics. Can I register for it?

Yes, you can register for **APS1112 – Applied Physics** (4 credits) in your current Semester 3.  

- First‑year courses (Semester 1 & 2) are offered in **both odd and even semesters**, so the parity rule does not block you.  
- The course’s parity evaluation confirms that registration is **PERMITTED**.  
- Register the course in **Mode A** (full attendance and appearance in all evaluation components), which is the standard requirement for clearing a backlog.  

Make sure the total credits you register for this semester do not exceed the 40‑credit limit.
I am a Computer Engineering student in semester 5. Can I register for AIC2042?

You cannot register for **AIC2042 – Principles of Machine Learning**. It is offered in Semester 4 (an even‑semester course), while you are currently in Semester 5 (odd). According to the registration rules, courses from an even semester are **strictly forbidden** to register for in an odd semester (except first‑year courses, which this is not).
Do NPTEL courses count towards my graduation credits, and how many minimum credits can I take online?

Yes. NPTEL (and other MOOC/SWAYAM) courses are accepted as Programme Elective (PE) or Open Elective (OE) credits toward graduation.

**Minimum online credit requirement:** 12 credits in total must be earned from online platforms (MOOC/NPTEL/SWAYAM). At least four PE/OE courses must be sourced from these platforms.

My CGPA is 9.2 but I had one backlog in the second semester. Am I eligible for Honours?

No, you are not eligible for Honours. Despite having a CGPA of 9.2, the fact that you had a backlog in the second semester disqualifies you from being considered for Honours. According to the rules, to be eligible for Honours, a student must pass every single course on the first attempt, with no backlogs or failures. Since you had a backlog, you do not meet this criterion, regardless of your high CGPA.
I am in semester 3 but I have a backlog in semester 1 Applied Physics. Can I register for it?

Yes, you can register for **APS1112 – Applied Physics** in your current Semester 3.

- **Parity:** The course is from an odd‑semester (Semester 1) and you are in an odd‑semester (Semester 3); the parity check confirms registration is permitted.  
- **First‑year exception:** Even if you were in an even semester, Semester 1/2 courses are offered in both odd and even semesters, so you would still be allowed to take the backlog.  
- **Registration mode:** Register the course in **Mode A** (fulfil attendance requirement and appear in all evaluation components). If you have already satisfied the attendance requirement for this course, you may also consider Mode B or Mode C, but Mode A is the default safe choice for a backlog.  
- **Credits:** The course carries **4 credits**, well within the maximum of **40 credits per semester**.  

Proceed with the registration as a backlog course in Mode A, and ensure you meet the attendance requirement for the theory component.

Provide a massive summary of all registration modes, promotion rules, and credit limits in one go.

**ZHCET Registration Overview (All Modes, Promotion Rules & Credit Limits)** | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Registration Modes** | • **Mode A** – Normal registration for all courses allotted to the student’s current semester (odd/even parity applies).
• **Mode B** – Registration for back‑log courses from previous semesters. First‑year (Sem 1 & 2) backlogs can be taken in **any** semester, regardless of parity.
• **Mode C** – Special registration for elective, audit, online (MOOC/NPTEL) or minor‑degree courses that are not part of the regular semester load. | | **Parity Rule** | • Odd semesters (1, 3, 5, 7) → only odd‑semester courses (except first‑year courses).
• Even semesters (2, 4, 6, 8) → only even‑semester courses (except first‑year courses). | | **Promotion & Continuation Criteria** | • **To Semester 3 or 4** – Minimum **16 earned credits** by the end of Semester II.
• **To Semester 5 or 6** – Minimum **60 earned credits**, with at least **36 credits** from the first two semesters, by the end of Semester IV.
• **To Semester 7 or 8** – Minimum **108 earned credits**, with at least **80 credits** from the first four semesters, by the end of Semester VI. | | **Penalty for Repeated Non‑Promotion** | • If a student is “Not Promoted” **more than three times**, admission is cancelled and the name is removed from the rolls. | | **Mercy Appeal** | • A removed student may appeal to the Vice‑Chancellor. If approved, the program duration can be extended by **up to two extra semesters** (maximum 14 semesters). | | **Credit Requirements** | • **Total graduation credits:** **180** (hard requirement).
• **Maximum credits per semester:** **40** (absolute cap; no exceptions). | | **Minor‑Degree Credits** | • Must comprise **24 – 30** additional credits beyond the major curriculum. | | **Online / MOOC Credits** | • Minimum **12 credits** from online platforms (MOOC/NPTEL) are mandatory for graduation; they count as Programme‑Elective (PE) or Open‑Elective (OE) credits. | | **Honours (First Division with Honours)** | • CGPA **≥ 8.5** **and** **no backlogs/failures** in any semester (first‑attempt pass in every course). Any backlog permanently disqualifies Honours. | | **First Division (without Honours)** | • CGPA **6.5 – 8.5** (backlogs allowed). | | **Branch‑Change Eligibility** | • CGPA **≥ 7.5** **and** seat availability in the desired branch. (Only relevant for branch‑change requests.) | **Key Take‑aways** - You can register for any first‑year backlog at any time (Mode B). - For all other backlogs, parity must be respected (odd ↔ odd, even ↔ even). - Never exceed **40 credits** in a semester; doing so is strictly prohibited. - To stay on track for graduation, accumulate at least **108 credits by end of Semester VI** and **180 credits total**. - Honours is only possible with a clean academic record; any backlog eliminates that possibility.
I have a 9.2 CGPA but I failed one lab in my 3rd semester and cleared it later. Can I graduate with Honours?

No. Even though your CGPA is well above 8.5, the fact that you had a failed lab (a backlog) in your 3rd semester permanently disqualifies you from Honours. Honours requires a CGPA ≥ 8.5 **and** a clean record with no backlogs or repeats.
How many 'additional' credits must I earn for a Minor Degree?
A Minor Degree requires **24 – 30 additional credits** beyond the credits needed for your major.
How many credits from MOOCS/NPTEL are mandatory for graduation, and which categories can they satisfy?
You must complete **at least 12 credits** through MOOC/NPTEL courses. These credits can be counted toward **Programme Elective (PE)** or **Open Elective (OE)** requirements.
I just finished my 4th semester. I have 65 total credits, but only 30 of them are from my 1st year. Am I promoted to the 5th semester?

You are **not promoted** to the 5th semester.

**Why:**  
- Promotion to Semester 5/6 requires **≥ 60 total earned credits** *and* **≥ 36 credits from the first two semesters** by the end of Semester IV.  
- You have 65 total credits (meets the 60‑credit threshold) but only **30 credits from your 1st‑year semesters**, which is below the required 36‑credit minimum.  

Therefore, you do not satisfy the promotion criteria for moving into Semester 5.

**Typical credit value for a Programme‑Core (PC) AI course:** 4 credits (most PC courses in the AI programme are 4‑credit theory courses; a few are 2‑ or 3‑credit labs, but the standard is 4 credits).

**Effect on the 40‑credit semester cap:** Adding a 4‑credit PC course will keep you within the 40‑credit limit **provided your current registered load is 36 credits or fewer**. | Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **CGPA** | Minimum 7.5 (at the end of the 2nd semester) |
| **Backlogs** | No backlogs allowed up to that point |
| **Merit/Seats** | Admission is merit‑based and depends on the availability of seats in the chosen minor |

A student has finished their 4th semester. They have earned 30 credits from their first year and 25 credits from their second year. Will they be promoted to the 5th semester? Explain the specific credit deficit based on the 108/80/60 rule.

No. The student will **not be promoted to the 5th semester**.

**Why – based on the 108 / 80 / 60 rule**

| Requirement for promotion to Semester 5/6 | Required | Student’s earned |
|--------------------------------------------|----------|------------------|
| **Total earned credits** (by end of Semester IV) | 60 credits | 55 credits |
| **Credits from the first two semesters** | 36 credits | 30 credits |

- **Total credit deficit:** 5 credits short of the required 60.  
- **First‑year credit deficit:** 6 credits short of the required 36 from Sem 1 + Sem 2.

Because both the overall credit minimum (60) **and** the minimum first‑year credit requirement (36) are not met, the student fails the promotion criteria for moving into Semester 5 (or 6).  

(For reference, promotion to Sem 7/8 later requires 108 total credits, with at least 80 from the first four semesters.)
If this is their third time being 'Not Promoted,' what is their last resort to stay in the program, and what is the absolute maximum time they have to graduate?

**Last‑resort option:**  
After the third “Not Promoted” status the student’s name is removed from the faculty rolls. The only way to stay in the program is to file a **Mercy Appeal to the Vice‑Chancellor**. If the appeal is approved, the university may extend the allowed study period.

**Absolute maximum time to graduate:**  
- Normal ceiling: **14 consecutive semesters** (the standard maximum).  
- With a successful Mercy Appeal: the period can be stretched by **up to two additional semesters**, giving an **absolute maximum of 16 semesters** (i.e., eight years).

I am repeating a course this semester because I failed the theory exam last year, but I had 80% attendance back then. If my current attendance drops to 40% due to an internship, can the department detain me from the End-Semester exam?

No. Because you already satisfied the attendance requirement (80 %) when you first took the course, the “repeating‑students exemption” applies: you will not be detained for low attendance in the repeat semester, even though your current attendance is only 40 %.  

You may therefore register the repeated theory course in **Mode B** (appear in all evaluation components) or **Mode C** (appear only for the end‑semester exam), as the repetition rules allow for either mode when the theory exam was failed but attendance was previously completed.
Since I'm repeating this theory course and already fulfilled attendance, which registration modes (b or c) are available to me, and how do they differ regarding sessional marks?

**Registration modes you can use**

| Mode | What you appear in | How sessional marks are treated |
|------|-------------------|---------------------------------|
| **Mode B** | All evaluation components (theory‑sessionals, practicals, end‑semester exam). | Sessionals are taken **again**; the new sessional marks replace the previous ones for that attempt. |
| **Mode C** | End‑semester exam only. | The **previous** sessional marks you earned earlier are retained and counted toward the final grade; you only sit the end‑semester exam again. |

Because you failed the theory exam but had already satisfied the attendance requirement, you are eligible to register the repeated course in **either Mode B or Mode C**. Choose Mode B if you want a chance to improve the sessional component, or Mode C if you prefer to keep the earlier sessional score and only retake the final exam.
